did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens with Abijah, Jeroboam’s son, falling ill, which leads Jeroboam’s wife to seek out the prophet Ahijah.
Did you know? Jeroboam told his wife to disguise herself so no one would recognize her as the king’s wife, and to go to Shiloh to see the prophet Ahijah.
Did you know? The gift Jeroboam’s wife was instructed to bring to Ahijah consisted of ten loaves of bread, cakes, and a jar of honey; Ahijah was to tell her what would happen to the boy.
Did you know? The prophet Ahijah was very old, and his eyes had become too dim for him to see.
Did you know? Although Jeroboam’s wife was disguised, Ahijah recognized her immediately because the Lord had told him beforehand who she was and what he should say to her.
Did you know? In the midst of the prophecy of disaster, it was said that only Abijah would receive a burial, because something good toward the Lord, the God of Israel, was found in him.

Did you know? The prophecy compares Israel to a reed swaying in the water and declares that the Lord would uproot Israel from the land and scatter them beyond the Euphrates because of their worship of the Asherahs.
Did you know? Jeroboam reigned over Israel for twenty-two years, and after his death his son Nadab succeeded him.
Did you know? In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign, Shishak king of Egypt marched against Jerusalem.
Did you know? Shishak took the treasures from the Lord’s temple and the royal palace, including the gold shields Solomon had made; Rehoboam later replaced them with bronze shields.
